name: Why? Channel
purpose: Individually authored episode questions and coverage boundaries for Why? Channel. The subject progression is organized by concrete content rather than a topic-by-angle multiplication.

topics.question: Why does a metal spoon often feel colder than a wooden spoon in the same room?
topics.coverage: Compare heat transfer, material properties and initial conditions using a safe observation; distinguish touch sensation from evidence that the objects have different starting temperatures.

topics.question: Why can a puddle disappear on a day that is not especially hot?
topics.coverage: Investigate evaporation, airflow, humidity and surface area with recorded conditions; avoid assuming temperature alone explains the rate.

topics.question: Why does a straw appear bent where it enters water?
topics.coverage: Explain refraction with a labeled ray diagram and safe original observations; distinguish optical appearance from the straw physically changing shape.

topics.question: Why can a spinning wheel seem to reverse direction on video?
topics.coverage: Compare sampling, periodic motion, frame rate and lighting through an original animation; do not infer actual reverse motion from recorded appearance.

topics.question: Why does condensation form on the outside of a cold glass?
topics.coverage: Trace water vapor, surface temperature and dew-point conditions; distinguish ambient moisture from liquid passing through the container.

topics.question: Why can two nearby places experience different rainfall during the same storm?
topics.coverage: Compare local observations, terrain and atmospheric conditions using official weather records; distinguish explanatory possibilities from a verified attribution of one event.

topics.question: Why does the Moon's shape appear to change through the month?
topics.coverage: Use official astronomy explanations and a labeled Sun-Earth-Moon model; distinguish phases from eclipses and avoid scale misleading the geometry.

topics.question: Why can a beach have more than one high tide in a day?
topics.coverage: Explain gravitational forcing, rotation and local basin response using official tidal references; do not turn an ideal model into a prediction for a specific shore.

topics.question: Why do mountain landscapes retain snow differently on different slopes?
topics.coverage: Compare elevation, sun exposure, wind and seasonal conditions with documented observations; distinguish contributing factors from a universal rule for every mountain.

topics.question: Why do some leaves change color before falling?
topics.coverage: Compare documented pigment changes, environmental cues and species differences; avoid implying all trees share one seasonal mechanism.

topics.question: Why can a seed remain ungerminated even when it receives water?
topics.coverage: Investigate species-specific dormancy, temperature, light and viability using botanical sources; exclude a universal germination recipe.

topics.question: Why do antibiotics not treat an ordinary viral infection in the same way as a susceptible bacterial infection?
topics.coverage: Use current official health guidance to distinguish targets, resistance and clinical decisions; exclude diagnosis, drug selection or advice to change prescribed treatment.

topics.question: Why can exercise make the heart beat faster without that alone establishing a health problem?
topics.coverage: Explain ordinary physiological demand with official sources and study limits; avoid interpreting a viewer's symptoms or offering individualized reassurance.

topics.question: Why does an almost-full storage device sometimes behave differently from an empty one?
topics.coverage: Inspect the actual storage technology, operating system and documented workload; distinguish possible causes rather than declaring one mechanism applies to every device.

topics.question: Why can a video look sharp while its file remains relatively small?
topics.coverage: Compare compression, redundancy, bitrate, content and viewing conditions using original clips; separate perceived quality from exact recovery of the source.

topics.question: Why can an elevator button light up before the elevator begins to move?
topics.coverage: Explain request registration, scheduling and system state through official diagrams; do not infer a malfunction or reveal access to control systems.

topics.question: Why can a microwave heat different parts of the same meal unevenly?
topics.coverage: Compare field distribution, food composition, geometry and manufacturer guidance; keep food-safety claims authoritative and exclude appliance modifications.

topics.question: Why can a place keep an old name after its political boundaries change?
topics.coverage: Trace official naming records, language use and local accounts for one named location; distinguish historical explanation from endorsing a contested territorial claim.

topics.question: Why do some languages assign grammatical gender to objects?
topics.coverage: Compare documented grammar systems and historical evidence in named languages; avoid treating grammatical categories as proof of speakers' beliefs about real-world gender.

topics.question: Why can the same historical event have different starting dates in different accounts?
topics.coverage: Inspect definitions, calendars, geographic scope and primary records; distinguish genuine periodization choices from demonstrable dating errors.

topics.question: Why do public institutions sometimes use procedures that appear slower than a direct personal decision?
topics.coverage: Choose one documented process and examine accountability, consistency, access and legal duties; avoid assuming every delay is justified or corrupt.

topics.question: Why can an average rise while many individual cases do not improve?
topics.coverage: Use a clearly illustrative dataset to compare mean, median, weighting and distribution; avoid disguising invented numbers as a real policy outcome.

topics.question: Why can a rare event become unsurprising when there are many opportunities for it?
topics.coverage: Explain trials, reference classes and simple probability with original examples; distinguish a model from evidence that any specific event was random.

topics.question: Why can two variables move together without one causing the other?
topics.coverage: Use labeled examples of confounding, reverse direction and selection; distinguish causal questions from a blanket dismissal of observational evidence.

topics.question: Why can a percentage change sound large while the absolute difference is small?
topics.coverage: Compare baselines, relative change and absolute counts with transparent invented data; keep denominators explicit and avoid a clinical or financial recommendation.

topics.question: When does a why question accidentally assume something that has not been established?
topics.coverage: Rewrite a false-premise example into observation, verification and explanation stages; distinguish checking the event from debating its possible causes.

topics.question: How can a causal explanation differ from an explanation of purpose?
topics.coverage: Compare a designed object, biological trait and social institution using attributed evidence; avoid assuming every feature exists because it was deliberately planned.

topics.question: What makes a popular single-cause explanation inadequate for a complex event?
topics.coverage: Map necessary conditions, contributing factors and alternatives in a bounded historical case; avoid replacing it with an equally unsupported all-causes narrative.

topics.question: How can a channel explain uncertainty without making every answer sound equally plausible?
topics.coverage: Compare evidence quality, competing predictions and confidence language in an original episode outline; distinguish unknown details from a complete absence of reliable knowledge.

topics.question: What should a why-channel demonstration establish before viewers treat it as proof?
topics.coverage: State setup, controlled conditions, measurement and limits for a harmless example; distinguish a visual analogy from an actual test of the explanation.

topics.question: How can an animated explanation avoid smuggling in the conclusion through its graphics?
topics.coverage: Identify assumed arrows, hidden forces, scale and timing in an original storyboard; anchor mechanisms in primary sources rather than persuasive motion alone.

topics.question: What should happen when a short explanation's missing exception changes the answer?
topics.coverage: Correct the claim, show the relevant conditions and update titles or captions; distinguish an acceptable simplification from a central error.

topics.question: How can a channel choose between a quick answer and a series of linked episodes?
topics.coverage: Use a question map with prerequisites, distinct subproblems and evidence needs; avoid multiplying a thin idea into repetitive videos solely to increase output.

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

science.requirements: Use original observations or experiments, an appropriate scientific reference and the actual measurement method. Distinguish mechanisms, correlations, model assumptions, uncertainty and limits of generalization.
source_leads: methods papers and current scientific reference works

synthesis.requirements: Define the rival claims and their evidence standards. Compare sources on equal terms, separate empirical findings from values or interpretations and do not imply that all positions have equal evidential support.
source_leads: the original sources behind the compared claims

media.requirements: Analyze an identifiable work or create a clearly labeled original example. Connect creative decisions to observable audience information; respect rights, attribution, consent and the difference between intent and reception.
source_leads: the actual work and authorized production materials
creator interviews or published craft explanations

history.requirements: Compare dated primary records, material evidence and historical scholarship. Distinguish event dates, the dates of surviving witnesses, later retellings and disagreement. Do not invent quotations, intentions or an unbroken lineage.
source_leads: dated archival records and original publications
inscriptions, artifacts or photographs with provenance
